name: Virtual Hand
summary: A direct 3D selection technique where the user controls a virtual hand to touch, grab, and manipulate nearby objects in the virtual environment.
howItWorks: Move the tracked hand or controller so that the virtual hand overlaps with the target object, then confirm the selection by grabbing, pressing a button, or performing a pinch gesture.
advantages: Natural selection and manipulation of nearby objects, especially when the interaction benefits from proprioception and direct hand-object contact.
limitations: Less suitable for distant targets because the user must reach toward the object or rely on an extended mapping. It can also cause fatigue during repeated or long interactions.
